<description>
**Problem:** The mempool estimator added in #34075 checks mempool health by comparing the weight of transactions removed from our mempool with the weight of recently mined blocks.
`removeForBlock` matches block transactions by txid, which does not commit to witness data.
If a block confirms a lighter witness variant than the one in our mempool, the estimator counts our heavier variant, so the health check can pass even when the matched transactions make up less than 75% of the mined weight.
A heavier mined variant has the opposite effect and understates coverage.
Same-txid witness variants also came up in #35501.

**Fix:** Count each matched transaction's weight from the connected block instead.
`removeForBlock` returns matches in block order, so the estimator can walk the block and the removed entries together.
The new test first records the false healthy result, then the corrected low-coverage result.
#36182 falls back to block policy for combined estimates when the mempool estimator cannot produce an estimate, but a false healthy result never reaches that fallback.
</description>

[2026-09-23] c:5793157228 comment by ismaelsadeeq (member):
Concept ACK.

This is an inherent false positive in master that also affects the `block_policy`,  too so https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34075 inherits it :(. Should be rare to occur to make a meaningful difference, but it should be fixed.

`removeForBlock` matches by txid, so when a block mines txid A with a different wtxid than the A we have in our mempool, `MempoolTransactionsRemovedForBlock` still reports our variant as the one that was mined.

The `mempool_policy` then miscounts its weight (this PR's concern), but the `block_policy` also records a false confirmation,  see `processBlockTx` it records our mempool variant's feerate bucket with a confirmation, but it's  actually a different transaction that we did not see propagate.

Rather than recomputing weight from the connected block, I think there's a cleaner fix that covers both, we should just filter at  `removeForBlock`: only record a tx removal as `BLOCK` on an exact wtxid match, and evict a witness mismatch as a `CONFLICT` instead via `TransactionRemovedFromMempool`.
[2026-09-23] c:5802096604 comment by l0rinc (member):
[quoted text omitted]

I considered changing `removeForBlock` instead of only the fee estimator, but treating a witness mismatch as `CONFLICT` also changes removal notifications and may count as a failure in block policy estimation so I would prefer doing that in a followup to avoid surprising side-effects.

This fix is more focused on the more urgent problem and also reuses each mined transaction’s weight in one block walk (instead of two iterations) and tests the coverage calculation, so I’d keep it focused and tackle removal separately.

Possible `txmempool.cpp` change

```diff
-                txs_removed_for_block.emplace_back(*it);
-                removeUnchecked(it, MemPoolRemovalReason::BLOCK);
+                const bool mined{it->GetTx().GetWitnessHash() == tx->GetWitnessHash()};
+                if (mined) txs_removed_for_block.emplace_back(*it);
+                removeUnchecked(it, mined ? MemPoolRemovalReason::BLOCK : MemPoolRemovalReason::CONFLICT);
```
</new_statements>
